\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تفریح} (tafrih)}{تفریح (tafrih)}]{\fa{تفریح} (tafrih) — recreation, fun; an outing}

\label{lesson:FA-C510-tafrih}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a die, then the Persian for to play cards.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تفریح}}
\textbf{\fa{تفریح}} (\emph{tafrih}) — \textquotedblleft{}recreation, fun; an outing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آخر} \fa{هفته} \fa{برای} \fa{تفریح} \fa{به} \fa{کوه} \fa{میرویم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{âkhar-e hafte barâ-ye tafrih be kuh miravim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the weekend we go to the mountains for fun.
\end{quote}

\emph{tafrih kardan} — to have fun, to go on an outing. Plural \emph{tafrihât}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tafrih} comes from Arabic \emph{tafrīḥ} (EtymDB), a word usually glossed 'cheering up, gladdening'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tafrih}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tafrih}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a die, then the Persian for to play cards, then say \emph{tafrih} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{وقت} \fa{گذراندن} (vaqt gozarândan)}{وقت گذراندن (vaqt gozarândan)}]{\fa{وقت} \fa{گذراندن} (vaqt gozarândan) — to spend time}

\label{lesson:FA-C510-vaqt-gozarandan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to play cards, then the Persian for recreation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{وقت} \fa{گذراندن}}
\textbf{\fa{وقت} \fa{گذراندن}} (\emph{vaqt gozarândan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to spend time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{با} \fa{نوه} \fa{هایش} \fa{وقت} \fa{میگذراند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u bâ navehâyash vaqt migozarânad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She spends time with her grandchildren.
\end{quote}

\emph{vaqt} 'time' + \emph{gozarândan} 'to pass (something)'; present stem \emph{gozarân-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vaqt gozarândan} is built in Persian on \emph{vaqt}, 'time', which was borrowed from Arabic \emph{waqt} (EtymDB), and native \emph{gozarândan}, 'to make pass', the causative of \emph{gozashtan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vaqt gozarândan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to play cards, then the Persian for recreation, then say \emph{vaqt gozarândan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرگرم} \fa{شدن} (sargarm shodan)}{سرگرم شدن (sargarm shodan)}]{\fa{سرگرم} \fa{شدن} (sargarm shodan) — to be absorbed (in); to be entertained}

\label{lesson:FA-C510-sargarm-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for recreation, then the Persian for to spend time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرگرم} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{سرگرم} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{sargarm shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be absorbed (in); to be entertained\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{با} \fa{بازی} \fa{سرگرم} \fa{شدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ bâ bâzi sargarm shodand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children got absorbed in the game.
\end{quote}

\emph{sargarm} 'busy, absorbed' (\emph{sar} 'head' + \emph{garm} 'warm') + \emph{shodan}. \emph{sargarmi} is a hobby.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sargarm shodan} is built on inherited words: \emph{sar}, 'head', and \emph{garm}, 'warm', which EtymDB traces back to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning 'to heat' (EtymDB), and \emph{shodan}, 'to become': a warm head, busy with something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sargarm shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sargarm shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for recreation, then the Persian for to spend time, then say \emph{sargarm shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خوش} \fa{گذشتن} (khosh gozashtan)}{خوش گذشتن (khosh gozashtan)}]{\fa{خوش} \fa{گذشتن} (khosh gozashtan) — to have a good time}

\label{lesson:FA-C510-khosh-gozashtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to spend time, then the Persian for to be absorbed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خوش} \fa{گذشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{خوش} \fa{گذشتن}} (\emph{khosh gozashtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to have a good time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{مهمانی} \fa{به} \fa{ما} \fa{خیلی} \fa{خوش} \fa{گذشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dar mehmâni be mâ kheyli khosh gozasht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We had a great time at the party.
\end{quote}

Impersonal: \emph{be man khosh gozasht} — 'it passed pleasantly for me'. Present stem \emph{gozar-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khosh gozashtan} is built on two native Persian words: \emph{khosh}, 'pleasant', and \emph{gozashtan}, 'to pass': time passed pleasantly. EtymDB has no entry for the phrase.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khosh gozashtan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khosh gozashtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to spend time, then the Persian for to be absorbed, then say \emph{khosh gozashtan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عضو} \fa{شدن} ('ozv shodan)}{عضو شدن ('ozv shodan)}]{\fa{عضو} \fa{شدن} ('ozv shodan) — to become a member, to join}

\label{lesson:FA-C510-ozv-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be absorbed, then the Persian for to have a good time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عضو} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{عضو} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{'ozv shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to become a member, to join\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{عضو} \fa{باشگاه} \fa{شطرنج} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u 'ozv-e bâshgâh-e shatranj shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He joined the chess club.
\end{quote}

\emph{'ozv} 'member; limb' + \emph{shodan}. Plural \emph{a'zâ} (Arabic).

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'ozv} comes from Arabic \emph{ʿuḍw} (EtymDB), a word for a limb and so a member of a body. \emph{shodan}, 'to become', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
